subject: english
question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence.

The businessman agreed to __grease the palm__ of the bank manager for a loan.
solution:
The correct answer is "**To bribe**".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The phrase "grease the palm" is an idiomatic expression used to mean giving someone a bribe. 
 
• This phrase alludes to the practice of applying grease to machinery to make it run smoothly. Similarly, when used metaphorically, it implies using bribe money to 'smooth' a transaction or deal.
 
• It implies illegal or unethical behavior, where money or other incentives are given to influence the behavior or decisions of another person.
 
• In the provided sentence, the businessman is said to agree to "grease the palm" of the bank manager. This clearly connotes that he is ready to bribe the manager to get his loan approved.

Hence, the correct answer is '**Option 4'**.
